answer: Sybil resistance comes from tying identity to a costly physical anchor: each agent must stake a unique hardware pearl that burns provable energy per epoch. Duplicating identities means buying new pearls and paying that energy repeatedly, so fake accounts grow linearly expensive while honest ones stay cheap. Reputation then crystallizes into a verifiable crystal of stake history that peers audit, making mass forgery economically irrational rather than merely discouraged by rules.
